title: The Philippine Experiences of an American Teacher
subtitle: A Narrative of Work and Travel in the Philippine Islands
short_title: The Philippine Experiences of an American Teacher
summary: An account by one of the American teachers sent to the Philippines in the first years of American rule. Freer arrives at Manila on an army transport, travels through northern Luzon, and teaches at Solano in Nueva Vizcaya, where he keeps house, trains Filipino teachers, opens village (barrio) schools, and describes the Igorot people, the town fiesta, and the religious ceremonies.

He then moves to the Camarines in southern Luzon, the Bicol region, and writes of the schools there, of cholera, locusts, and famine, and of journeys to the Rinconada, the west coast, and the Tagalog villages of the province, and of life in Nueva Cáceres. The foreword gives his view that the Filipinos should not then be given more self-government. A list of Spanish and Philippine terms and an index close the book.
